passages.text: And the LORD said to Moses, “If someone sins and acts unfaithfully against the LORD by deceiving his neighbor in regard to a deposit or security entrusted to him or stolen, or if he extorts his neighbor or finds lost property and lies about it and swears falsely, or if he commits any such sin that a man might commit— once he has sinned and becomes guilty, he must return what he has stolen or taken by extortion, or the deposit entrusted to him, or the lost property he found, or anything else about which he has sworn falsely. He must make restitution in full, add a fifth of the value, and pay it to the owner on the day he acknowledges his guilt.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
He gave Moses a command.
If a person sins, he acts unfaithfully against the LORD.
He may deceive his neighbor about something entrusted to him.
He may lie about a deposit or a security.
He may steal from his neighbor.
He may extort his neighbor.
He may find lost property and lie about it.
He may swear falsely about any of these things.
He may commit any sin like these that people do.
If he sins and becomes guilty, he must act.
He must return what he stole.
He must return what he took by extortion.
He must return the deposit entrusted to him.
He must return the lost property he found.
He must return anything about which he swore falsely.
He must pay back the full amount.
He must add a fifth of its value.
He must give it to the owner on the day he admits his guilt.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃ נֶ֚פֶשׁ כִּ֣י תֶחֱטָ֔א וּמָעֲלָ֥ה מַ֖עַל בַּיהוָ֑ה וְכִחֵ֨שׁ בַּעֲמִית֜וֹ בְּפִקָּד֗וֹן אֽוֹ־ בִתְשׂ֤וּמֶת יָד֙ א֣וֹ בְגָזֵ֔ל א֖וֹ עָשַׁ֥ק אֶת־ עֲמִיתֽוֹ׃ אֽוֹ־ מָצָ֧א אֲבֵדָ֛ה וְכִ֥חֶשׁ בָּ֖הּ וְנִשְׁבַּ֣ע עַל־ שָׁ֑קֶר עַל־ אַחַ֗ת מִכֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־ יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה הָאָדָ֖ם לַחֲטֹ֥א בָהֵֽנָּה׃ וְהָיָה֮ כִּֽי־ יֶחֱטָ֣א וְאָשֵׁם֒ וְהֵשִׁ֨יב אֶת־ הַגְּזֵלָ֜ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר גָּזָ֗ל א֤וֹ אֶת־ הָעֹ֙שֶׁק֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׁ֔ק א֚וֹ אֶת־ הַפִּקָּד֔וֹן אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָפְקַ֖ד אִתּ֑וֹ א֥וֹ אֶת־ הָאֲבֵדָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר מָצָֽא׃ א֠וֹ מִכֹּ֞ל אֲשֶׁר־ יִשָּׁבַ֣ע עָלָיו֮ לַשֶּׁקֶר֒ וְשִׁלַּ֤ם אֹתוֹ֙ בְּרֹאשׁ֔וֹ וַחֲמִשִׁתָ֖יו יֹסֵ֣ף עָלָ֑יו לַאֲשֶׁ֨ר ה֥וּא ל֛וֹ יִתְּנֶ֖נּוּ בְּי֥וֹם אַשְׁמָתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Then he must bring to the priest his guilt offering to the LORD: an unblemished ram of proper value from the flock.
passages.sermon:
The guilty person must bring an offering to the LORD.
He must bring this offering to the priest.
He must choose a ram from the flock.
The ram must be unblemished.
The ram must be of proper value.
This ram is the guilt offering.
passages.original: וְאֶת־ אֲשָׁמ֥וֹ יָבִ֖יא לַיהוָ֑ה אַ֣יִל תָּמִ֧ים מִן־ הַצֹּ֛אן בְּעֶרְכְּךָ֥ לְאָשָׁ֖ם אֶל־ הַכֹּהֵֽן׃

passages.text: In this way the priest will make atonement for him before the LORD, and he will be forgiven for anything he may have done to incur guilt.”
passages.sermon:
The priest stands before the LORD.
The priest makes atonement for the person.
God forgives the person.
God forgives every sin that made the person guilty.
passages.original: וְכִפֶּ֨ר עָלָ֧יו הַכֹּהֵ֛ן לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה וְנִסְלַ֣ח ל֑וֹ עַל־ אַחַ֛ת מִכֹּ֥ל אֲשֶֽׁר־ יַעֲשֶׂ֖ה לְאַשְׁמָ֥ה בָֽהּ׃פ

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Command Aaron and his sons that this is the law of the burnt offering: The burnt offering is to remain on the hearth of the altar all night, until morning, and the fire must be kept burning on the altar.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD gave Moses a command.
The LORD told Moses to command Aaron and his sons.
Aaron was the high priest.
Aaron’s sons were priests.
The LORD said, “This is the law of the burnt offering.
The burnt offering must stay on the hearth of the altar all night.
It must remain there until morning.
The fire on the altar must keep burning.
Do not let the fire go out.”
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃ צַ֤ו אֶֽת־ אַהֲרֹן֙ וְאֶת־ בָּנָ֣יו לֵאמֹ֔ר זֹ֥את תּוֹרַ֖ת הָעֹלָ֑ה הִ֣וא הָעֹלָ֡ה עַל֩ מוֹקְדָ֨ה עַל־ הַמִּזְבֵּ֤חַ כָּל־ הַלַּ֙יְלָה֙ עַד־ הַבֹּ֔קֶר וְאֵ֥שׁ הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ תּ֥וּקַד בּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And the priest shall put on his linen robe and linen undergarments, and he shall remove from the altar the ashes of the burnt offering that the fire has consumed and place them beside it.
passages.sermon:
The priest serves God at the altar.
The priest must put on his linen robe.
The priest must also put on linen undergarments next to his skin.
The priest must remove the ashes from the burnt offering on the altar.
The fire has consumed the burnt offering.
The priest must take these ashes.
The priest must place the ashes beside the altar.
passages.original: וְלָבַ֨שׁ הַכֹּהֵ֜ן מִדּ֣וֹ בַ֗ד וּמִֽכְנְסֵי־ בַד֮ יִלְבַּ֣שׁ עַל־ בְּשָׂרוֹ֒ וְהֵרִ֣ים אֶת־ הַדֶּ֗שֶׁן אֲשֶׁ֨ר תֹּאכַ֥ל הָאֵ֛שׁ אֶת־ הָעֹלָ֖ה עַל־ הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ וְשָׂמ֕וֹ אֵ֖צֶל הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

passages.text: Then he must take off his garments, put on other clothes, and carry the ashes outside the camp to a ceremonially clean place.
passages.sermon:
The priest must remove his special garments.
He must put on other clothes.
He must take the ashes from the altar.
He must carry the ashes outside the camp.
He must place the ashes in a clean place.
passages.original: וּפָשַׁט֙ אֶת־ בְּגָדָ֔יו וְלָבַ֖שׁ בְּגָדִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים וְהוֹצִ֤יא אֶת־ הַדֶּ֙שֶׁן֙ אֶל־ מִח֣וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה אֶל־ מָק֖וֹם טָהֽוֹר׃

passages.text: The fire on the altar shall be kept burning; it must not be extinguished. Every morning the priest is to add wood to the fire, arrange the burnt offering on it, and burn the fat portions of the peace offerings on it.
passages.sermon:
The fire must burn on the altar.
No one may let the fire go out.
The priest must add wood to the fire every morning.
The priest must place the burnt offering on the fire.
The priest must burn the fat from the peace offerings on the fire.
passages.original: וְהָאֵ֨שׁ עַל־ הַמִּזְבֵּ֤חַ תּֽוּקַד־ בּוֹ֙ לֹ֣א תִכְבֶּ֔ה וּבִעֵ֨ר עָלֶ֧יהָ הַכֹּהֵ֛ן עֵצִ֖ים בַּבֹּ֣קֶר בַּבֹּ֑קֶר וְעָרַ֤ךְ עָלֶ֙יהָ֙ הָֽעֹלָ֔ה וְהִקְטִ֥יר עָלֶ֖יהָ חֶלְבֵ֥י הַשְּׁלָמִֽים׃

passages.text: The fire shall be kept burning on the altar continually; it must not be extinguished.
passages.sermon:
God commanded the priests of Israel to keep a fire burning on the altar.
The altar stood in the Tabernacle.
The fire must burn at all times.
The priests must never let the fire go out.
passages.original: אֵ֗שׁ תָּמִ֛יד תּוּקַ֥ד עַל־ הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ לֹ֥א תִכְבֶֽה׃ס

passages.text: Now this is the law of the grain offering: Aaron’s sons shall present it before the LORD in front of the altar.
passages.sermon:
The law of the grain offering is as follows.
Aaron’s sons are priests.
The priests must bring the grain offering.
They must bring it before the LORD.
They must bring it to the front of the altar.
passages.original: וְזֹ֥את תּוֹרַ֖ת הַמִּנְחָ֑ה הַקְרֵ֨ב אֹתָ֤הּ בְּנֵֽי־ אַהֲרֹן֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־ פְּנֵ֖י הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

passages.text: The priest is to remove a handful of fine flour and olive oil, together with all the frankincense from the grain offering, and burn the memorial portion on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The priest serves God at the altar.
The priest takes a handful of fine flour from the grain offering.
The priest also takes some olive oil from the grain offering.
The priest gathers all the frankincense that is on the grain offering.
The priest burns this portion on the altar.
This portion is called the memorial portion.
The smoke rises from the altar.
The aroma pleases the LORD.
passages.original: וְהֵרִ֨ים מִמֶּ֜נּוּ בְּקֻמְצ֗וֹ מִסֹּ֤לֶת הַמִּנְחָה֙ וּמִשַּׁמְנָ֔הּ וְאֵת֙ כָּל־ הַלְּבֹנָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־ הַמִּנְחָ֑ה וְהִקְטִ֣יר הַמִּזְבֵּ֗חַ רֵ֧יחַ נִיחֹ֛חַ אַזְכָּרָתָ֖הּ לַיהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Aaron and his sons are to eat the remainder. It must be eaten without leaven in a holy place; they are to eat it in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.
passages.sermon:
Aaron and his sons serve as priests.
They must eat what remains of the grain offering.
They must eat it as unleavened bread.
They must eat it in a holy place.
They must eat it in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.
passages.original: וְהַנּוֹתֶ֣רֶת מִמֶּ֔נָּה יֹאכְל֖וּ אַהֲרֹ֣ן וּבָנָ֑יו מַצּ֤וֹת תֵּֽאָכֵל֙ בְּמָק֣וֹם קָדֹ֔שׁ בַּחֲצַ֥ר אֹֽהֶל־ מוֹעֵ֖ד יֹאכְלֽוּהָ׃

passages.text: It must not be baked with leaven; I have assigned it as their portion of My offerings made by fire. It is most holy, like the sin offering and the guilt offering.
passages.sermon:
God gave instructions for the grain offering.
The priests must not bake it with leaven.
God assigned this portion to the priests from His offerings made by fire.
This portion is most holy.
It is like the sin offering.
It is like the guilt offering.
passages.original: לֹ֤א תֵאָפֶה֙ חָמֵ֔ץ חֶלְקָ֛ם נָתַ֥תִּי אֹתָ֖הּ מֵאִשָּׁ֑י קֹ֤דֶשׁ קָֽדָשִׁים֙ הִ֔וא כַּחַטָּ֖את וְכָאָשָֽׁם׃

passages.text: Any male among the sons of Aaron may eat it. This is a permanent portion from the offerings made by fire to the LORD for the generations to come. Anything that touches them will become holy.”
passages.sermon:
Aaron had sons.
Aaron’s sons could be priests.
Any male among Aaron’s sons may eat this offering.
This offering comes from the sacrifices made by fire to the LORD.
This rule is permanent.
This rule will last for all generations.
Anything that touches these offerings will become holy.
passages.original: כָּל־ זָכָ֞ר בִּבְנֵ֤י אַהֲרֹן֙ יֹֽאכֲלֶ֔נָּה חָק־ עוֹלָם֙ לְדֹרֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם מֵאִשֵּׁ֖י יְהוָ֑ה כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־ יִגַּ֥ע בָּהֶ֖ם יִקְדָּֽשׁ׃פ

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “This is the offering that Aaron and his sons must present to the LORD on the day he is anointed: a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a regular grain offering, half of it in the morning and half in the evening.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD gave Moses instructions.
Aaron is the high priest.
Aaron has sons who serve as priests.
Aaron and his sons must bring an offering to the LORD.
They must do this on the day Aaron is anointed as priest.
The offering is a grain offering.
They must use a tenth of an ephah of fine flour.
This offering is regular and required.
They must offer half of the flour in the morning.
They must offer the other half in the evening.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃ זֶ֡ה קָרְבַּן֩ אַהֲרֹ֨ן וּבָנָ֜יו אֲשֶׁר־ יַקְרִ֣יבוּ לַֽיהוָ֗ה בְּיוֹם֙ הִמָּשַׁ֣ח אֹת֔וֹ עֲשִׂירִ֨ת הָאֵפָ֥ה סֹ֛לֶת מִנְחָ֖ה תָּמִ֑יד מַחֲצִיתָ֣הּ בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וּמַחֲצִיתָ֖הּ בָּעָֽרֶב׃

passages.text: It shall be prepared with oil on a griddle; you are to bring it well-kneaded and present it as a grain offering broken in pieces, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The grain offering must be prepared with oil.
You must cook it on a griddle.
You must knead the offering well.
You must bring the offering in pieces.
You must present it as a grain offering to the LORD.
The offering will have a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
passages.original: עַֽל־ מַחֲבַ֗ת בַּשֶּׁ֛מֶן תֵּעָשֶׂ֖ה מֻרְבֶּ֣כֶת תְּבִיאֶ֑נָּה תֻּפִינֵי֙ מִנְחַ֣ת פִּתִּ֔ים תַּקְרִ֥יב רֵֽיחַ־ נִיחֹ֖חַ לַיהוָֽה׃

passages.text: The priest, who is one of Aaron’s sons and will be anointed to take his place, is to prepare it. As a permanent portion for the LORD, it must be burned completely.
passages.sermon:
Aaron has sons.
One son will become priest after Aaron.
This son will be anointed.
The anointed son will prepare the offering.
This rule is permanent.
The offering belongs to the LORD.
Burn the offering completely.
passages.original: וְהַכֹּהֵ֨ן הַמָּשִׁ֧יחַ תַּחְתָּ֛יו מִבָּנָ֖יו יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֹתָ֑הּ חָק־ עוֹלָ֕ם לַיהוָ֖ה כָּלִ֥יל תָּקְטָֽר׃

passages.text: Every grain offering for a priest shall be burned completely; it is not to be eaten.”
passages.sermon: A priest brings a grain offering.\r\nThe priest must burn the entire offering.\r\nNo one may eat any part of it.
passages.original: וְכָל־ מִנְחַ֥ת כֹּהֵ֛ן כָּלִ֥יל תִּהְיֶ֖ה לֹ֥א תֵאָכֵֽל׃פ

passages.text: And the LORD said to Moses, “Tell Aaron and his sons that this is the law of the sin offering: In the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered, the sin offering shall be slaughtered before the LORD; it is most holy.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD gave Moses a message.
The LORD told Moses to speak to Aaron and his sons.
The LORD said, “This is the law of the sin offering.
You must slaughter the sin offering in the same place as the burnt offering.
You must slaughter it before the LORD.
The sin offering is most holy.”
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃ דַּבֵּ֤ר אֶֽל־ אַהֲרֹן֙ וְאֶל־ בָּנָ֣יו לֵאמֹ֔ר זֹ֥את תּוֹרַ֖ת הַֽחַטָּ֑את בִּמְק֡וֹם אֲשֶׁר֩ תִּשָּׁחֵ֨ט הָעֹלָ֜ה תִּשָּׁחֵ֤ט הַֽחַטָּאת֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה קֹ֥דֶשׁ קָֽדָשִׁ֖ים הִֽוא׃

passages.text: The priest who offers it shall eat it; it must be eaten in a holy place, in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.
passages.sermon:
The priest offers the sin offering.
That priest must eat the offering.
He must eat it in a holy place.
He must eat it in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.
passages.original: הַכֹּהֵ֛ן הַֽמְחַטֵּ֥א אֹתָ֖הּ יֹאכֲלֶ֑נָּה בְּמָק֤וֹם קָדֹשׁ֙ תֵּֽאָכֵ֔ל בַּחֲצַ֖ר אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃

passages.text: Anything that touches its flesh will become holy, and if any of the blood is spattered on a garment, you must wash it in a holy place.
passages.sermon:
God gave laws about the sin offering.
The sin offering is most holy.
Anything that touches the flesh of the sin offering becomes holy.
If blood from the sin offering falls on a garment, you must wash that garment.
You must wash the garment in a holy place.
passages.original: כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־ יִגַּ֥ע בִּבְשָׂרָ֖הּ יִקְדָּ֑שׁ וַאֲשֶׁ֨ר יִזֶּ֤ה מִדָּמָהּ֙ עַל־ הַבֶּ֔גֶד אֲשֶׁר֙ יִזֶּ֣ה עָלֶ֔יהָ תְּכַבֵּ֖ס בְּמָק֥וֹם קָדֹֽשׁ׃

passages.text: The clay pot in which the sin offering is boiled must be broken; if it is boiled in a bronze pot, the pot must be scoured and rinsed with water.
passages.sermon:
A clay pot may be used to boil the sin offering.
The priest must break the clay pot after using it.
A bronze pot may also be used to boil the sin offering.
The priest must scour the bronze pot after using it.
The priest must rinse the bronze pot with water.
passages.original: וּכְלִי־ חֶ֛רֶשׂ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תְּבֻשַּׁל־ בּ֖וֹ יִשָּׁבֵ֑ר וְאִם־ בִּכְלִ֤י נְחֹ֙שֶׁת֙ בֻּשָּׁ֔לָה וּמֹרַ֥ק וְשֻׁטַּ֖ף בַּמָּֽיִם׃

passages.text: Any male among the priests may eat it; it is most holy.
passages.sermon: The priests are men.\r\nAny male priest may eat this offering.\r\nThis offering is most holy.
passages.original: כָּל־ זָכָ֥ר בַּכֹּהֲנִ֖ים יֹאכַ֣ל אֹתָ֑הּ קֹ֥דֶשׁ קָֽדָשִׁ֖ים הִֽוא׃

passages.text: But no sin offering may be eaten if its blood has been brought into the Tent of Meeting to make atonement in the Holy Place; it must be burned.
passages.sermon:
A sin offering is a sacrifice for sin.
Sometimes, the priest brings the blood of the sin offering into the Tent of Meeting.
The priest brings the blood to make atonement in the Holy Place.
If the blood of the sin offering is brought into the Tent of Meeting for atonement in the Holy Place, no one may eat the offering.
The priest must burn the entire offering with fire.
passages.original: וְכָל־ חַטָּ֡את אֲשֶׁר֩ יוּבָ֨א מִדָּמָ֜הּ אֶל־ אֹ֧הֶל מוֹעֵ֛ד לְכַפֵּ֥ר בַּקֹּ֖דֶשׁ לֹ֣א תֵאָכֵ֑ל בָּאֵ֖שׁ תִּשָּׂרֵֽף׃פ
